extracted.intended_audience: authors, illustrators, translators, and publishers submitting children's books to the SCBWI Golden Kite Awards (SCBWI members)
extracted.subtask_description: Submission and eligibility guidelines for entering books in the SCBWI Golden Kite Awards (children's literature) for books published in 2026, including category definitions, member and publisher requirements, format and deadline rules, and prize information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication year eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: You may apply as an author, illustrator, or translator of a book INITIALLY published in 2026. The book submitted must be published in 2026.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries are limited to books initially published in the specified year (2026).

rubrics_metrics.name: Membership requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: You must be a current member through December 2026 to have a book submitted to the Golden Kite Awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only current SCBWI members (through the stated date) may have books submitted on their behalf.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Only books written or translated into English are accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All submissions must be in English, whether originally written in English or translated into English.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publisher eligibility and submission channel
rubrics_metrics.description: Books must be published by PAL publishers. The best way to submit to the Golden Kites is in conjunction with your publisher; publishers will be emailed guidelines directly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Individuals should contact their publisher to check if the book has been submitted and ask the publisher to submit copies on their behalf. If a publisher is unable to submit, contact the Golden Kite Coordinator for further instructions. Publishers can contact [email protected] for questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical-copy submission policy (individuals)
rubrics_metrics.description: Physical copies sent in by individuals will not be accepted as of 2024.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not mail physical copies yourself; submissions should go through publishers unless instructed otherwise by the awards coordinator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format requirement (bound copies only)
rubrics_metrics.description: All submissions MUST BE in completed, bound form. NO GALLEYS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unbound proofs, galleys, or incomplete formats are not acceptable; submit only final, bound books.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission deadlines and publisher shipping
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions will not be accepted after October 31. Publishers must ship out entries no later than Monday, November 3.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Meet the submission cut-off date (Oct 31) and ensure publishers ship copies by the stated latest shipping date (Nov 3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Category limits and multi-category exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: You may submit your book to ONE category only, except in the case of Picture Book Text, Picture Book Illustration, and Illustrated Books for Older Readers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: the same book can be submitted for Illustrated Books for Older Readers for the illustrator and for Middle Grade for the author, but both the author and the illustrator must be current members. Use the allowed exceptions judiciously; otherwise choose one category per book.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation category eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: To be eligible for the Translation category, please submit a book translation that was initially published in English in 2026. It may have been translated from any other language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This category is for translations published in English in the eligibility year, regardless of the source language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-published books exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Self-published books are not eligible for the Golden Kite Awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Independently published books may instead be entered in the Spark Award (a separate program).

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepted categories and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: The Golden Kite Awards recognize books in eight categories: Picture Book Text; Picture Book Illustration; Illustrated Books for Older Readers (includes graphic novels, fiction, and nonfiction for middle grade and young adult illustrated books); Middle Grade; Young Adult; Nonfiction Text for Younger Readers; Nonfiction Text for Older Readers; Translation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check category definitions carefully (e.g., 'Illustrated Books for Older Readers' explicitly includes graphic novels and illustrated fiction/nonfiction for middle grade and YA) to select the appropriate category.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission roles allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: You may apply as an author, illustrator, or translator of a book.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions can be made on behalf of any of these contributor roles, subject to membership and publisher-submission rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of awards and honors per category / publicity
rubrics_metrics.description: One Golden Kite Award Winner and Honor book will be chosen per category. Each category winner receives $2,500, while honor recipients are awarded $500.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Winning books will be showcased at the SCBWI booth at the Bologna Children's Book Fair, included in a press release and an announcement on the SCBWI website and social media, and each winner will receive gold stickers for their books.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advisory council entry policy (conflict handling)
rubrics_metrics.description: Although SCBWI advisory council members are eligible to enter their books in the Golden Kites, the advisory council have decided that should any of them win, they will donate the prize money to a nonprofit organization of their choice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Council members may participate but have an internal policy to avoid retaining prize funds if they win.
